sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, and it is created lazily on first access.
sketches.resonance: Declaring someone as an `object` means the language itself guarantees there will never be another — uniqueness enforced by the compiler.

sketches.mechanism: A value moved into a closure cannot be used afterward — the borrow checker enforces that giving something away means you no longer have it.
sketches.resonance: The compiler makes the cost of giving literal: once you move what you had into someone else's scope, reaching for it again is an error.

sketches.mechanism: A LEFT JOIN preserves every row from the left table even when no matching row exists on the right — unmatched columns fill with NULL.
sketches.resonance: Staying present even when the other side has nothing to offer, and carrying the absence as NULL — that is what loyalty looks like in a query.
sketches.draft:
SELECT self.day, other.reply
FROM   every_day self
LEFT JOIN responses other
ON     self.day = other.day;
